key_insight: Placing trainable nonlinear functions on the connections of analogue neural networks makes them much better at representing smooth continuous targets than conventional weight-only physical networks.
engineering_relevance: This could enable ultra-low-power edge control and energy-management hardware, with a projected CMOS implementation around 30 µW and hardware-friendly analogue realizations.
method: Use Kolmogorov-Arnold-inspired connections with trainable nonlinear functions instead of scalar weights.
Implement the nonlinear connections as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Validate transfer of trained networks to hardware and compare against MLPs and memristive simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved efficiency on smooth tasks such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, with quantified transfer across about 35,000 connections.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and does not extend to classification-like decision boundaries, so it is not a universal replacement for standard neural architectures.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
